candidate.answerReason: The light drops 1/0.5 = 2 m per horizontal metre. Across 6 m it drops 12 m, so the flagpole height is 12 + 2 = 14 m.

methods.label: Constant vertical drop
methods.explanation: The light rays descend \(1\text{ m}\) for every \(0.5\text{ m}\) forward, or \(2\text{ m}\) for every \(1\text{ m}\) horizontally. Over the horizontal distance of \(6\text{ m}\) from the top of the flagpole to the wall, they descend \(12\text{ m}\). Thus, the height of the flagpole is \(2+12=14\text{ m}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses an elementary constant ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance, with no trigonometry required.
